item.title: Police seek public’s help after burglary at Sumrall Pharmacy - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
SUMRALL – The Sumrall Police Department is asking for the public’s help as officers investigate a burglary at Sumrall Pharmacy.

Police said the break-in happened shortly after midnight Sunday, April 19. The Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics is also assisting in the investigation.

According to the department, surveillance footage shows two people entering the business through a rear window while another person remained outside. Authorities said the suspects later fled on foot into a nearby field.

Police are asking anyone who recognizes the individuals or has information about the burglary to contact the Sumrall Police Department at 601-758-3531 or by email at [email protected] .

Anonymous tips can also be submitted to Crime Stoppers at 601-582-STOP.

item.title: Person killed in shooting outside Jackson liquor store - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Capitol Police are investigating a shooting Tuesday afternoon at a liquor store on E. Northside Drive that left one person dead. The liquor store is called Liquor Wine and Spirits.

Officers responded at about 12:23 p.m. to the business after receiving a report of a shooting, according to Capitol Police.

When officers arrived, they found one person dead at the scene. No arrests had been made as of Tuesday afternoon.

Capitol Police are asking anyone with information about the shooting to call 601-359-3125.

No additional details were immediately released.

item.title: On Earth Day, learn about the Great Mississippi Nature Trail - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — On Earth Day, Mississippi leaders and conservation advocates are encouraging residents to step outside and explore the landscapes that have long defined the state’s identity.

From winding rivers and cypress-filled bayous to pine forests and rolling hills, Mississippi’s outdoors tell a story of ecosystems that have shaped communities and sustained generations. The Great Mississippi Nature Trail brings many of those landscapes together, offering access to natural areas, state parks, wildlife refuges and scenic trails across the state.

The trail connects destinations ranging from waterfalls and rail trails to quiet wilderness areas, showcasing Mississippi’s ecological diversity and cultural history.

“Happy Earth Day,” the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce posted on Facebook Wednesday. “There’s no better time to celebrate Native Plant Month than by getting outside and discovering the beauty of Mississippi’s natural landscape.”

When most people think of Mississippi, they picture the Delta, the blues, or the Mississippi River itself. But tucked along the Great Mississippi Nature Trail is a botanical world full of carnivorous plants, ancient cypress groves, and some of the most diverse native flora in the entire country.

If you’re interested in a starting point, go with Crosby Arboretum in Picayune. This 104-acre native plant conservatory is home to more than 700 species of trees, shrubs, wildflowers, and grasses, and that’s just the interpretive center. Wander into the pitcher plant bogs and you’ll find yourself face to face with some of nature’s most clever survivors. Sundews have a sticky “dew” designed to trap unsuspecting insects. Parrot pitcher plants, which are compact little carnivorous plants only four to six inches tall, sit quietly waiting for their next meal.

Head north and watch the landscape shift noticeably. At Leroy Percy State Park, huge oaks draped in Spanish moss frame artesian springs that have been flowing for centuries. At Tishomingo State Park, swamp cypress trees line Bear Creek against a backdrop of sandstone bluffs.

In the Delta, the Yazoo National Wildlife Refuge and Delta National Forest tell a different story: one of bottomland hardwoods, where oak, ash, elm, and cottonwood form a canopy that supports white-tailed deer, wild turkey, and hundreds of migratory bird species.

What ties all of these places together is Mississippi’s extensive plant diversity. The state is home to roughly 200 native tree species alone, from longleaf pine in the piney woods of the south to hardwood forests in the north. Some of the rarest plants in the country — bog flax, bog spicebush, and native orchids — cling to existence in the Gulf Coast’s wet pine savannas, where less than 3% of the original habitat remains.

The Great Mississippi Nature Trail is a chance to see the state’s wild side before it disappears. Officials said the trail provides opportunities for all types of visitors, whether they are planning a family outing, a scenic drive or a weekend on the water.

Popular stops along the route include state parks such as LeFleur’s Bluff State Park, Tishomingo State Park and Percy Quin State Park, as well as federal sites like the Natchez Trace Parkway and the Noxubee National Wildlife Refuge. Local favorites such as the Longleaf Trace and unique natural landmarks like Red Bluff also draw visitors each year.

Advocates say spending time outdoors is not only a way to celebrate Earth Day, but also a way to build a deeper connection to the environment.

The Department of Agriculture and Commerce encouraged Mississippians to explore areas where native plants thrive, noting that understanding local ecosystems can help residents make more sustainable choices at home.

For those planning a trip, officials recommend bringing plenty of water, checking trail conditions ahead of time and following “Leave No Trace” principles to protect natural resources. Spring and fall are often considered the best times to visit, offering milder weather and increased wildlife activity. Activities along the trail range from hiking and fishing to kayaking and wildlife viewing, with many sites designed to accommodate families through accessible boardwalks and rail trails.

As Earth Day underscores the importance of conservation, leaders say Mississippi’s natural spaces remain both a resource and a responsibility.

By exploring the state’s outdoors, they say, residents can better appreciate the landscapes that make Mississippi unique and help ensure they are preserved for future generations.

item.title: Man shot at home on Jones Avenue in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Capitol Police are investigating a shooting Thursday afternoon at a residence on Jones Avenue in Jackson that left one person injured.

Officers responded at about 3:32 p.m. to a report of a shooting, according to Capitol Police.

When officers arrived, they found one person suffering from an apparent gunshot wound to the leg.

The victim was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. No arrests had been made as of Thursday afternoon.

Capitol Police are asking anyone with information to call 601-359-3125.

item.title: Louisville Police invite community to Law Enforcement Torch Run for Special Olympics - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
LOUISVILLE — The Louisville Police Department is inviting residents to take part in its annual Law Enforcement Torch Run in support of Special Olympics athletes.

The event is scheduled for May 5 at 11:30 a.m. at the safe room on North Columbus Avenue, where community members are encouraged to participate by running, walking or cheering along the route.

Officials said the Torch Run is designed to raise awareness and show support for Special Olympics participants while bringing the community together.

Organizers said children will be present to cheer on participants, and the event is expected to provide a day of fun and community spirit.

The department encouraged residents to attend, noting that community involvement plays a key role in supporting Special Olympics athletes.

item.title: Five inmates injured during incident at Central MS Correctional Facility - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – Several inmates were injured during an incident this week at the Central Mississippi Correctional Facility in Rankin County, according to WLBT.

WLBT reported that a Mississippi Department of Corrections representative said the agency is investigating the incident, which happened Monday, April 20.

According to WLBT, five inmates were taken to a local hospital for treatment. Three of those inmates have since been released.

The condition of the other two inmates was not provided.

item.title: DARKHORSE DOGS: Dusty is a playful young dog who loves life and is looking for a home - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON, Miss. — Community Animal Rescue and Adoption has the sweetest dog up for adoption named Dusty. This young dog has brought the shelter energy and joy since the day he arrived.

According to CARA, Dusty was found in Jackson after a woman came across a pack of stray dogs. The other dogs ran off, but Dusty jumped into the woman’s car and rode with her to the shelter with his tail wagging.

CARA said Dusty has been happy and affectionate since arriving in November.

The dog is just over a year old, according to the shelter. He weighed 36 pounds when he first arrived and was up to 50 pounds at his last weigh-in.

Shelter staff describe Dusty as energetic, playful and loving. CARA said he enjoys playing with other dogs, running in the dog park and spending time with people. He is a shelter favorite and this good boy deserves the BEST home.

Dusty is available for meet-and-greet appointments! Hurry and go meet this sweet guy! Call the shelter at 601-922-7575.

People interested in adopting him can find more information and an application through the shelter’s website.

item.title: Clinton to hold spring citywide cleanup April 25 through May 2 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLINTON – The City of Clinton will hold its annual Spring Citywide Cleanup from April 25 through May 2, giving residents a free way to dispose of yard waste, bulky items and household debris.

The cleanup site will be open daily from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., except Sunday, April 26, when it will be closed, according to the city.

The drop-off location will be at Old Northside Elementary School, 1111 Old Vicksburg Road. City employees will be on site throughout the week to assist residents.

Officials said residents should line up on Longwood Place in the Briars and turn west onto Old Vicksburg Road for disposal.

The service is limited to Clinton residents because of program costs, the city said. Residents must show proof of residency with either a City of Clinton water or garbage bill or a driver’s license with a Clinton address.

The city said it will not accept electronic waste such as computers, printers and keyboards, or refrigerators, freezers and air conditioning units containing freon.

Residents with questions can call 601-924-2239.

item.title: City of Ridgeland appoints Paul Forster to Metro Jackson Water Authority Board - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
RIDGELAND — The City of Ridgeland is pleased to announce the appointment of Paul Forster, City Engineer, as its representative on the newly established Metro Jackson Water Authority Board. Forster will serve as a member-at-large, appointed by Mayor Gene McGee and confirmed by the Board of Aldermen.

The Metro Jackson Water Authority, created through the Metro Jackson Water Authority Act, is expected to assume oversight of Jackson’s water and sewer systems following the conclusion of the current federal receivership. The nine-member governing board will include appointments from multiple jurisdictions, including the City of Jackson, the Governor’s Office, the Lieutenant Governor, and the mayors of Ridgeland and Byram.

Forster brings extensive experience in civil engineering and public service. Prior to joining Ridgeland, Forster served as City Engineer and Director of Engineering and Utilities for the City of Flowood, and now serves as Ridgeland’s City Engineer. In that role, he oversaw a wide range of operations including utility management, capital improvement planning, construction oversight, budgeting, personnel management, and regulatory compliance.

In his role with the City, Forster supports key areas including transportation, water and sewer infrastructure, environmental initiatives, and community development, ensuring the City continues to meet the demands of growth while maintaining high standards of service. Mr. Forster has extensive experience in utility management, capital improvement planning, construction oversight, budgeting, personnel management, and regulatory compliance. He also serves on the Commission for the City of Jackson 1% Special Sales Tax.

“We are looking forward to serving the entirety of the jurisdiction on this authority, and we hope to contribute to the success of the entire metro area through our efforts,” said Forster.

The City of Ridgeland looks forward to supporting the Metro Jackson Water Authority and working collaboratively with regional partners to strengthen water and wastewater services for the entire community.

item.title: 18-wheeler leaves scene after collision with train in Wiggins - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WIGGINS – An 18-wheeler collided with a train Friday afternoon at a railroad crossing in Wiggins before leaving the scene, according to the Wiggins Fire Department.

Firefighters responded at about 1 p.m. to the crossing on South 1st Street between East Fifth Avenue and Mill Avenue after reports of a crash involving a train and a tractor-trailer.

When crews arrived, the train was stopped on the tracks and showed no visible damage, according to the fire department.

According to the train crew, the 18-wheeler crossed the tracks without stopping, and the train’s engine struck the rear portion of the trailer.

The truck left the scene before emergency responders arrived.

The Wiggins Police Department later located and stopped the 18-wheeler. The driver reported no injuries, according to the fire department.

Minor injuries were reported among members of the train crew, but no one needed to be taken by ambulance.

The crash remains under investigation by local law enforcement and other appropriate authorities.

The Wiggins Fire Department reminded drivers to come to a complete stop at all railroad crossings and look both ways before proceeding.
